q: A youth picked at 9 PM is kept in station till next evening without any court production. Family alleges illegal custody. What is the lapse?
options: No lapse until 48 hours pass
Must be produced before magistrate within 24 hours excluding travel time; detention beyond is illegal
Production needed only after confession
SHO can extend custody orally for 7 days
expl: Production within 24 hrs excluding journey is mandatory.
why: Prompt judicial oversight checks police custody. Every extra hour without remand makes detention unconstitutional.
trapnote: Trap: counts 48 hours or seeks confession first.

q: Constables bring a woman theft accused at 11:30 PM, arrested without lady constable or magistrate nod. Your check?
options: Approve as routine night patrol arrest
Flag violation: woman's night arrest needs exceptional ground plus prior magistrate permission and lady officer presence
Send her to judicial lockup without papers
Release only on political recommendation
expl: Night safeguard bars sunset-sunrise arrest of woman except exceptionally with prior permission and woman police.
why: Safeguard protects dignity and prevents misuse. SI must refuse irregular custody and re-arrest lawfully if needed.
trapnote: Trap: treats night arrest of woman as normal.

q: Family says a boy is secretly held in a farmhouse by rivals with police connivance. Which court relief should you advise them to seek urgently?
options: Order to produce the person and test legality of detention
Order directing authority to do neglected public duty
Order questioning a person's claim to public office
Order transferring pending case between courts
expl: By function that is habeas corpus: produce body, examine cause.
why: Writs are chosen by function, not name. Illegal confinement needs production, not a direction for file disposal.
trapnote: Trap: pushes mandamus for any police lapse.

q: An NGO files public interest plea on custodial beatings after you report pattern injuries. SHO says NGO has no locus. Your legal position?
options: PIL not maintainable in criminal matters
PIL relaxes standing for public injury; cooperate with court notice and preserve records
Destroy medico-legal register to protect station
Arrest petitioners for defamation
expl: PIL allows third-party standing for oppressed/unreachable victims.
why: Courts widened access for systemic violations. Retaliation or record tampering invites contempt and criminal liability.
trapnote: Trap: insists only victim can move court.

q: Village sarpanch asks you to audit panchayat grant spending and punish secretary on the spot. What is correct scope?
options: SI audits accounts and convicts secretary
Audit of public accounts is by CAG with report to legislature; police only register/investigate cognizable offence if disclosed
Ignore complaint as CAG bars FIR
Seize panchayat funds without case
expl: CAG audits state accounts and reports to legislature.
why: Audit and policing are separate accountability tracks. Conflating them derails both financial oversight and fair probe.
